details.publicNotes:
On rare occasions, a woodpluck develops a particularly powerful imagination, significantly strengthening their power to cultivate and manifest whatever they can dream up. These woodpluck elders often become leaders in their communities. They can cultivate large and intricate constructions from their minds, such as rideable beasts, and to a woodpluck, the iconic image of an elder is atop the back of a majestic imagined creature. When woodpluck communities are threatened, elders lead choruses into battle to defend their homes.

Though elders are respected for their creativity and prowess alike, few use that influence to rule outside of emergency situations. After all, spending considerable time on the responsibilities of leadership would interfere with their ability to engage with the joy of creation. Woodpluck elders often seek inspiration beyond the boundaries of their home villages, wandering to settlements that are home to a variety of ancestries and eagerly trading crafting ideas with anyone who catches their eye.

Woodplucks are plump fey creatures with a single arm protruding from their torsos. Their eager imaginations manifest in physical form through a small plant sprout embedded in each individual's head, which grows and shapes itself into whatever the host woodpluck is thinking about at the time. When a woodpluck sleeps, their sprout's roots dig into their mind and grow out into the most vivid scenes of their dreams.

Woodplucks can gather in choruses to work together, and when their imagination grows, they can become powerful elders.

Junior Elders

Despite their title, woodpluck elders aren't necessarily the longest-tenured members of their community. Many so-called woodpluck elders are young adults or even children whose outsized imaginations make them the envy of their seniors. No matter their age, the inventions of woodpluck elders often incorporate many childlike elements: hobby horses and cuddly dragons are common.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 64/140/250 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (piercing, slashing), armor (medium), skill items (Acrobatics, Crafting, Deception, Diplomacy, Nature, Performance)

Eligible Imbued Properties bane, charisma, constitution, dexterity, energy resistant (vitality), light, mind, mind shield, sensory (low-light vision), spells (Primal: @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.IihxWhRfpsBgQ5jS]{Enthrall}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.tlSE7Ly8vi1Dgddv]{Laughing Fit}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.0qaqksrGGDj74HXE]{Revealing Light}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.KsWhliKfUs3IpW3c]{Wall of Thorns}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-anachronism.spells.8M03UxGXjYyDFAoy]{Weapon Storm}), strength, tangle shield, throwing, wild, wisdom, wood

Area 30-foot cone or 10-foot emanation

You swing a weapon you're holding, and the weapon magically multiplies into duplicates that swipe at all creatures in either a cone or an emanation. This flurry deals four dice of damage to creatures in the area. This damage has the same type as the weapon and uses the same die size. Determine the die size as if you were attacking with the weapon; for instance, if you were wielding a two-hand weapon in both hands, you'd use its two-hand damage die.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage.

Failure The target takes full damage.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage and is subject to the weapon's critical specialization effect.

Heightened (+1) Add another damage die.

Your words fascinate your targets. You speak or sing without interruption throughout the casting and duration. Targets who notice your speech or song might give their undivided attention; each target must attempt a Will save. The GM might grant a circumstance bonus (to a maximum of +4) if the target is of an opposing religion, ancestry, or political leaning, or is otherwise unlikely to agree with what you're saying.

Each creature that comes within range has to attempt a save when you Sustain the spell. If you're speaking, enthrall gains the linguistic trait.

Critical Success The target is unaffected and notices that you tried to use magic.

Success The target needn't pay attention but doesn't notice you tried to use magic (it might notice others are enthralled).

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} with you. It can attempt another Will save if it witnesses actions or speech with which it disagrees. If it succeeds, it's no longer fascinated and is temporarily immune for 1 hour. If the target is subject to a hostile act, or if another creature succeeds at a Diplomacy or Intimidation check against it, the fascination ends immediately.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target can't attempt a save to end the fascination if it disagrees with you.

You grow a wall of thorny brambles from the ground. You create a 5-foot-thick wall of brambles and thorns in a straight line up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high. You must create the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost. The wall stands vertically. If you wish, the wall can be of a shorter length or height. Everything on each side of the wall has cover from creatures on the opposite side, and the wall's spaces are difficult terrain. For every move action a creature uses to enter at least one of the wall's spaces, that creature takes 3d4 piercing damage.

Each 10-foot-by-10-foot section of the wall has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 20 Hit Points. It's immune to critical hits and precision damage. A destroyed section can be moved through freely.

Heightened (+1) The Hit Points of each section of the wall increase by 5, and the piercing damage increases by 1d4.

The target is overtaken with uncontrollable laughter. It must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is plagued with uncontrollable laughter. It can't use reactions.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} and can't use reactions.

Critical Failure The target falls @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} and can't use actions or reactions for 1 round. It then takes the effects of a failure.

A wave of magical light washes over the area. You choose the appearance of the light, such as colorful, heatless flames or sparkling motes. A creature affected by revealing light is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled}. If the creature was @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} instead. If the creature was already concealed for any other reason, it is no longer concealed.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The light affects the creature for 2 rounds.

Failure The light affects the creature for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The light affects the creature for 10 minutes.

The woodpluck merges their body into an adjacent tree. While merged, they can't take any actions that require their body (including Cultivate Imagination), but they can still use their mind and senses as normal while merged. They can exit the tree into any space adjacent to the tree as a two-action activity, ending the effect.
When a woodpluck wields a melee weapon they created with Cultivate Imagination, the weapon produces splinters on impact, dealing an additional 1d8 piercing damage.

The woodpluck imagines a common non-magical weapon, shield, piece of adventuring gear, or simple tool of up to level 3 and no more than 3 Bulk, which then grows on their head. Any weapon created with this ability is a +1 striking weapon and gains the effects of a returning rune if it has the thrown trait. A woodpluck elder can wield a weapon that requires two hands in its one hand. The cultivated item is made entirely from wood and other plant matter, but otherwise functions as the base item. The woodpluck can then Interact to grab the item. The most common weapons imagined by woodplucks are listed in their Strikes above. Cultivating an item in this way causes any items previously created by the woodpluck's imagination to break down into ordinary plant matter.

The woodpluck imagines a Medium or Large creature or simple vehicle, which then grows from a secondary sprout to form a wooden mount underneath it. The elder's size increases to that of the imagined creature, and the elder chooses to either increase its Speed to 40 feet or gain a fly Speed of 25 feet. The mount is an extension of the elder, not a separate creature. The elder can Dismiss this effect.

Requirements The woodpluck elder has a Cultivated Mount

Effect The woodpluck elder jumps off their mount and sends it charging forward, dealing @Damage[8d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage to creatures and unattended objects in an @Template[type:line|distance:80]. Creatures in the line must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:26] save. If the mount collides with an object or creature of a size larger than it, the line stops early unless the object or creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points, After the charge, the mount breaks down into ordinary plant matter.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is knocked @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage, is knocked prone, and becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 minute.
